title: Building Reactive AI Apps: Matt Welsh
talk_summary: Matt Welsh presents Fixie's open-source AI.JSX framework, a React-like TypeScript library for composing LLM applications as trees of components that render asynchronously and in parallel to the LLM. The talk is primarily a product announcement and demo (RAG in ~10 lines, tool invocation, realtime voice drive-through demo) with little measured evidence or operational detail.

takeaways.what_they_do: Compose an LLM app as a tree of components; sibling components render concurrently, each streaming tokens into the parent's prompt as they arrive.
takeaways.evidence_quote: all three of those components are going to run in parallel and they're all streaming in parallel there's three concurrent llm calls

takeaways.technique: Wrapper components as reusable prompt transforms
takeaways.what_they_do: A 'kid-safe' wrapper component injects a system message and rewrites any child component's output, so a constraint is applied by composition instead of editing each prompt.
takeaways.evidence_quote: when we just wrap any component we want in a kids safe component it automatically will rewrite the output to be kidsafe

takeaways.what_they_do: A doc-QA component retrieves chunks for the query and inlines them into the system message of a chat-completion component, all in one declarative tree.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the docs QA component Returns the chunks that are relevant to that query places them right there in the system message

takeaways.what_they_do: Tools are declared as a named record with an English description plus a JS function, and only components nested under a use-tools wrapper can invoke them.
takeaways.evidence_quote: instantiate a used tools component give it that set of tools and then anything that might need to use those tool tools
